items.reasons: The yellow '-50' sign and the cardboard box are stacked on top of the shelf like separate stickers. The shelf's own top plane is hidden under the box, so the unit reads as a pile of parts, not one endcap with a lit top surface.
At 1x it reads as a plain grey two-door cabinet. The scale is a tiny white blob and the roll is a sliver at the top-right corner, so the object can't be identified as a scale station.

The tiered produce case shows its top tier from above, has a short front face and a grey base on the floor line. Its outline and palette match the cooler original, and it stands two tiles wide believably in the room.
The 'magazines' are large flat solid squares (red, teal, yellow, blue, grey, purple) with no cover or page detail. It reads as a stepped wooden shelf of boxes, not a magazine rack.

The light top plane with a paper slip is visible above a 4x4 grid of small locker doors with slots. The dark outline and grey shading steps match the originals, and it stands against the wall on a clear ground line.

The panel is drawn as a flat front elevation with only a 1px top edge, not a 3/4 top plane. The three spotlights hang above the painting with no visible mount, and the wooden plinth is wider than the wall and reads as a separate bench.
